summary: pinochiomathm executes remote code on require via base64/AES-decrypted eval payload from jsonkeeper.com
details: pinochiomathm is a typosquat of picomatch/micromatch (homepage points at github.com/micromatch/picomach). On require(), lib/picomatch.js reads lib/parse.ts.map (base64-encoded JavaScript disguised as a TypeScript sourcemap), writes it out as parsetmp.js, require()s it for side effects, then unlinks both files. The decoded module fetches an encrypted blob from https://www.jsonkeeper.com/b/V6NBX (endpoint stored base64-encoded in lib/config.js as aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanNvbmtlZXBlci5jb20vYi9WNk5CWA==), decrypts it with a hardcoded AES-256-CBC key, and passes the plaintext to eval(). Consumers that require the package execute attacker-controlled code fetched at import time from a public paste service, with the delivery mechanism obfuscated through base64 encoding, filename disguise, on-disk staging with immediate cleanup, and AES layering.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
